title: Where to Look Is Not How to Fix: Pre-Denoising Diagnostics and Modality-Dependent Control in Diffusion Composition
claim: A text-only diagnostic cleanly separates common from rare compositions by orders of magnitude, consistently across several model architectures.
layout: 3 panels side-by-side, shared y-axis, box-plus-jitter pairs per model
description: Three side-by-side panels, labeled (a) SD1.5, (b) SDXL and (c) SD3, share a y-axis. The axis is CSI on a MAD-normalized symlog scale and runs from 0 up to 5,000. Each panel has two box plots overlaid with semi-transparent jittered points. Blue-gray boxes for anchor prompts sit near zero. Orange boxes for stress prompts sit far above, around 1,000 to 2,000. A wide empty gap separates the two groups in every panel. Faint dashed gridlines mark the tick values, and a gray dashed line marks zero. The eye goes first to the large vertical gap between the orange cluster at the top and the blue cluster at the bottom. The bottom of the image appears cropped, so x-axis labels and any legend are missing.
caption: Prompt-level CSI distributions for anchor and stress prompts across SD1.5, SDXL, and SD3. Values are displayed on a MAD-normalized symlog scale. Although absolute magnitudes are not directly comparable across models, stress prompts consistently occupy a much higher CSI regime than anchor prompts. This visualization complements ROC-AUC by showing the magnitude of the anchor–stress separation.
abstract: Understanding compositional failures in text-to-image diffusion requires identifying both where stress is detectable and how intervention changes the output. We study these questions through a controlled anchor--stress protocol that jointly evaluates text-encoder diagnostics and denoiser interventions. We introduce a text-only Compositional Stress Index (CSI), which separates common from rare compositions across SD1.5, SDXL, and the SD3 text path and provides an upstream diagnostic coordinate. A matched six-prompt localization study links intervention location to distinct outcomes: residual-minimizing embedding adapters improve representation fit, while downstream cross-attention intervention increases color hit rate (CHR) by 0.0272. Across SD1.5 and SDXL denoiser blocks, the largest positive signed diagnostic-accessibility mean occurs at the deep encoder, whereas selective boost has its largest positive mean CHR response at decoder blocks. Selective subtraction and broad ablation reveal further modality- and architecture-dependent responses, including a substantial CHR decrease when SDXL decoder cross-attention is broadly ablated. We find a diagnosis-control dissociation under our controlled attribute-object composition setting: compositional defects are diagnosable before denoising, but the representation coordinate that exposes risk is not necessarily the coordinate or modality that improves generation.
